input.rationale: Two open limitations of the current account are directly testable with the same scenario: whether an invocation issued with a context that never expires stays pending, and whether a still-pending invocation is admitted once an observed leader change re-arms the run loop's gate (and whether its payload then commits). A native dry run of the corrected harness suggested yes for all three, so a successor experiment is submitted for retained evidence. This batch also answers the four follow-up gaps registered by the knowledge-1 correction: they concern whether that premise correction changes the evidence or conclusions of its recorded uses.

interpretations.rationale: Mechanism statement corrected in the previous revision; evidence unchanged. In 87b38a551d554c2391427dda00c4e6e4, node 3 applied its own re-admission (index 4) and its configuration listed it as a voter with leader 1 (index 5); the admitted invocation (index 6) had not returned after 1200 ms (index 7), released only at the caller's deadline (index 8: 'context deadline exceeded', 2501 ms), and left its payload absent from every node's committed entries (index 9). During the same stable-leader period the never-removed member's invocation returned in 0 ms and committed on all three nodes (indices 11, 12); two independent retries on node 3 (indices 14, 19) also never completed and were not committed, while in each interval a fresh proposal by node 2 returned in 0 ms and committed on all three nodes (indices 17, 22); after the leader change 1->2 at term 2 (index 23) a new invocation on node 3 returned in 0 ms and committed (indices 25, 26). Source account: the run loop's gate variable is assigned only at node.go:374/377/426 and used as the receive case at node.go:386, and a re-admission cannot match the removal guard because the local Progress entry is already gone (node.go:401-412), so the caller's send on n.propc (node.go:525) stays pending while no leader change is observed. The snapshot's own expectation (node_test.go:352-385) scopes intended blocking to a node that does not know the current leader, which is not this case; the control and interval controls exclude cluster-wide stalls, and the post-leader-change call excludes a defect in node 3's state machine. Net effect: a member's proposal duty is held pending without any error signal for as long as no leader change is observed, and the successor experiment submitted in this batch tests whether that pending duty is admitted by a later leader change and whether the unbounded case stays pending.

The receipt contains no leader change inside the pending window, so the corrected premise is consistent with the observed release at the caller's deadline.

scope.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API in one process. Node 1 campaigns and becomes leader in the initial configuration {1,2,3} supplied by the storage ConfState; committed remove-3 and add-3 conf changes are proposed on the leader and applied on every node. Then the experiment issues, on re-added node 3: the witness invocation (2500 ms context), an invocation with a context that never expires (observed for 2000 ms), and two retry attempts (900 ms contexts) each paired with a proposal by never-removed node 2 committed in the same interval; it also runs the control on node 2, then forces a leader change to node 2 at term 2 and issues a further invocation on node 3, and finally observes whether the context-free invocation was admitted by the re-armed gate and whether its payload committed. Every invocation records whether it returned, the error, elapsed time, the node's observed voter status and leader, and whether the payload reached any node's committed entries.
assumptions: Message delivery between the three in-process nodes is reliable and ordered per sender; no ticks are delivered, so leader 1 stays stable until the experiment forces the leader change.
Storage appends of Ready.Entries happen before the Ready's messages are dispatched.

The removal and re-addition are the committed conf changes the driver applies; node 3 applies both through Node.ApplyConfChange. The context-free invocation is issued before any leader change and is not cancelled by the harness, so its admission can only come from the run loop re-arming its receive side.

experiment.prefix: Start nodes 1,2,3 with a MemoryStorage per node whose ConfState voters are {1,2,3} (captured test helper withPeers). Node 1 campaigns at term 1 and becomes leader; every node then reports leader 1 and node 1 has applied the initial entry. Propose a remove-3 ConfChange on node 1 and wait until node 3's applied entries contain it and node 3's configuration excludes node 3 (voter=false). Propose an add-3 ConfChange on node 1 and wait until node 3's applied entries contain it and node 3's configuration includes node 3 again (voter=true) with leader still 1. Then run the witness invocation, the context-free invocation, the control, the two retry/progress intervals, and the forced leader change with the final invocation and the post-re-arm observations on node 3.

The state machine would have accepted the proposal (stepFollower forwards to the leader) and the removed-leader case returns ErrProposalDropped instead of blocking (raft.go:1298-1302), so no rejection or loss is reported to the caller while the member is in fact a voter with a known leader.
